summary: Backend-only retest after anti-clone changes to POST /api/auth/device. (1) Re-ran /app/backend_test.py end-to-end: 35/35 PASS. (2) Authored /app/backend/tests/test_anti_clone_device_auth.py with 6 focused pytest cases covering the four requested scenarios + 2 negative checks: ALL 6 PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1500+ lines — consider splitting into modules (auth, admin, tasks, wallet, referrals) for maintainability. Not blocking.

Anti-clone match order in /api/auth/device is correct: exact device_id OR device_ids[] -> fingerprint -> create. The $addToSet to device_ids when a clone is detected guarantees subsequent re-installs from either ANDROID_ID resolve to the same user.
device_fingerprint is not indexed. With user growth, the fingerprint lookup will scan the users collection. Recommend adding a sparse index on device_fingerprint (and on device_ids) for production.
seed_data_creation: Tests create disposable users via /api/auth/device with random uuid device_ids and random fingerprints. No persistent seed data added; canonical admin record (user_id=admin_altaff) reused via 93altaff@gmail.com login. No cleanup needed because device users are anonymous.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Anti-clone tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_anti_clone_device_auth.py and can be re-run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_anti_clone_device_auth.py -v`. Full regression: `python /app/backend_test.py` (35 cases). Both green on https://mint-app.preview.emergentagent.com against current server.py.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs surfaced. The 4 requested behaviours are correctly implemented in /api/auth/device: (a) same fingerprint + new device_id reuses the existing user_id and appends the new device_id to device_ids[] (clone defence works), (b) different fingerprint creates a fresh user_id, (c) exact device_id match still resolves to the existing user even when a different fingerprint is sent, (d) requests without a fingerprint fall back to pure device_id matching (legacy clients unaffected).
